agent: reader B of the trade and aid wave (2026-10-13): the Lua the trade and aid scripts reach
question: Every engine class, method, constructor and constant Their Finest Hour's ai_trade.lua (ProposeTrades, EvalutateExistingTrades, DiploScore_OfferTrade), ai_license.lua and the debt and lend-lease DiploScore functions reach that FINDINGS-luaapi.md does not cover: what each answers and in what unit; how a script posts an offer and what it becomes; what the extra arguments of DiploScore_OfferTrade and DiploScore_LicenceTechnology are.

addresses.name: CTradeAction_Construct
addresses.signature: CTradeAction* __stdcall CTradeAction_Construct(CTradeAction* self, CCountryTag actor, CCountryTag recipient)
addresses.comment: **The C++ constructor behind the Lua expression `CTradeAction(actor, recipient)`** - the one the shipped scripts use; CTradeAction::Create (0x4E8F50) is the other, registered as the static `Create`, and builds the same object. 0xA34A60 to the `ret 0x14` at 0xA34B4D; the object on the stack, not in ECX, so recorded as a free function (trap 11). One caller, LuabindConstruct_CTradeAction (0x5880B0), which allocated 0xB0 bytes. Writes persistent id 0x18D, actor at +0x8/+0xC, recipient at +0x10/+0x14, type 0 (PROPOSE), date and last_command_date both the game state's tick (+0xBDC), value (+0x24) 1, the vftable 0x15FB8D4, and builds the embedded route at +0x28 through the CTradeRoute constructor 0xA4C4F0 with **EDX = the actor and ECX = the recipient**, which that constructor stores as the route's `from` (+0x24) and `to` (+0x2C). So in every action a script makes, the route's from is the actor and its to the recipient, and both goods vectors start at nought.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA34A60..0xA34B4D: the stores at 0xA34AF9..0xA34B1B and the vftable write at 0xA34B30; the route constructor's argument registers at 0xA34B2A/0xA34B2D and the constructor's own stores of *EDX to +0x24 and *ECX to +0x2C (Ghidra, 0xA4C4F0). findRefs --callers: one call, from 0x988122. Wrong if the route constructor's register roles were the other way round, which its decompilation of the two stores would show.

addresses.name: CLicenceTechnologyAction_Construct
addresses.signature: CLicenceTechnologyAction* __stdcall CLicenceTechnologyAction_Construct(CLicenceTechnologyAction* self@ESI, CCountryTag actor@stack:4, CCountryTag recipient@stack:0xC) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The C++ constructor behind the Lua expression `CLicenceTechnologyAction(buyer, seller)`**, which Support_License.ProductionCheck in ai_license.lua uses. The object in ESI, the two tags by value on the stack, `ret 0x10` at 0xA3B4BE. One caller, LuabindConstruct_CLicenceTechnologyAction (0x58A3D0), which allocated **0x38 bytes** - the class's size. Writes persistent id 0x18D, actor +0x8/+0xC, recipient +0x10/+0x14, type 0, date and last_command_date the tick, value 1, vftable 0x15FB994, and **zeroes Subunit (+0x28), Serial (+0x2C), Paralell (+0x30) and Money (+0x34)** - so a licence a script makes is for no unit, none of them, at no price, until its setters run.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA3B3E0..0xA3B4BE, the stores at 0xA3B475..0xA3B4AD; findRefs --callers: one call, 0x98A440; the 0x38 is the operator new at 0x98A415. Wrong if 0x98A3D0 were not the luabind construct for this class - its type descriptor chain (function_object_impl<construct<CLicenceTechnologyAction,...>> at 0x172D2B0, vftable 0x15F1F9C, slot 1 0x9392F0 -> 0x985640 -> 0x98A3D0) says it is.

addresses.name: LuabindConstruct_CTradeAction
addresses.signature: void __stdcall LuabindConstruct_CTradeAction(void* self_argument, CCountryTag actor, CCountryTag recipient)
addresses.comment: luabind's `construct<CTradeAction, std::auto_ptr<CTradeAction>, (argument const&, CCountryTag, CCountryTag)>`: what `CTradeAction(a, b)` in Lua runs once overload resolution (0x9767F0, reached from the function_object_impl vftable 0x15F153C slot 1, 0x934A40) has picked it. Takes the instance userdata out of the self argument, `operator new(0xB0)`, CTradeAction_Construct (0x634A60) with the two tags **by value**, and installs the object in the userdata as an auto_ptr holder - so **the action belongs to Lua and is collected with it**. That is safe because CEU3AI::PostAction posts a clone (CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand clones through slot 16), never the object itself. `ret 0x14` at 0x988189.
addresses.evidence: type descriptor 0x1735880 (.?AU?$function_object_impl@U?$construct@VCTradeAction@@V?$auto_ptr@VCTradeAction@@...) -> COL 0x16331FC -> vftable 0x15F153C, slot 1 = 0x934A40 -> call 0x9767F0 -> call 0x9880B0 at 0x976952; inside, push 0xB0 / call 0xB9602F / call 0xA34A60. Wrong if 0x9767F0 called another constructor on a different overload - it has one call to a construct body.

addresses.name: LuabindConstruct_CLicenceTechnologyAction
addresses.signature: void __stdcall LuabindConstruct_CLicenceTechnologyAction(void* self_argument, CCountryTag actor, CCountryTag recipient)
addresses.comment: luabind's `construct<CLicenceTechnologyAction, std::auto_ptr<...>, (argument const&, CCountryTag, CCountryTag)>`: `operator new(0x38)` and CLicenceTechnologyAction_Construct (0x63B3E0), the object held by Lua through an auto_ptr. Reached from the function_object_impl vftable 0x15F1F9C slot 1 (0x9392F0) through the overload entry 0x985640. `ret 0x14` at 0x98A4A7.
addresses.evidence: type descriptor 0x172D2B0 -> COL 0x16300B4 -> vftable 0x15F1F9C, slot 1 0x9392F0 -> 0x985640 -> call 0x98A3D0 at 0x9857A2; inside, push 0x38 / call 0xB9602F / call 0xA3B3E0 at 0x98A440. Wrong if the size pushed were not the object's - CLicenceTechnologyAction_Construct's last store is +0x34, four bytes, which fits 0x38 exactly.

addresses.name: LuabindConstruct_CFixedPointFromFloat
addresses.comment: **What `CFixedPoint(x)` in Lua makes of a number** - the constructor FINDINGS-luaapi.md left unread. The overload entry (0x9673F0) takes the Lua number with lua_tonumber and **stores it as a single-precision float** (`fstp dword` at 0x9674D0) before calling here. Then `operator new(4)` and: `t = (float)((double)f + 0.0005)` (the double at 0x160A460 is the float 0.0005 widened), `u = (float)((double)t * 1000.0)` (0x160A300), `floorf(u)` (0x401FD0) and `_ftol2_sse` - so **thousandths = floor((float)((float)(f + 0.0005) * 1000))**, the same fx(f) as the operators with a number (FINDINGS-luaapi.md, section 3): to the nearest thousandth with a half going up, through single precision. CFixedPoint(-2.5) is -2500, CFixedPoint(0.0004) is 0 and CFixedPoint(-0.0004) is -1. The object is held by Lua. `ret 4` at 0x987D6F.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x987CDE..0x987D15 (cvtps2pd / addsd [0x160A460] / cvtpd2ps / cvtss2sd / mulsd [0x160A300] / cvtpd2ps / floorf / _ftol2_sse / mov [esi], eax); 0x9674CA..0x9674E2 in the overload entry (lua_tonumber, fstp dword, movss to the stack argument). Reached from type descriptor 0x1741DA0 (construct<CFixedPoint, auto_ptr, (argument const&, float)>) -> vftable 0x15F0388 slot 1 0x92EB20 -> 0x9673F0 -> call 0x987CA0 at 0x9674F2. Wrong if the double at 0x160A460 were not 0.0005 - it reads 0.0005000000237.

addresses.name: LuaCallProxy_OfferTrade_CallIntResult
addresses.comment: The seven-argument twin of LuaCallProxy_CallIntResult (0x644080), for `DiploScore_OfferTrade`: sets the proxy's called flag (+0x28), pushes the arguments through LuaPushArgs_OfferTrade (0x644D50), calls `[proxy+8]` (luabind::detail::pcall) with **(L, 7, 1)**, throws luabind::error on a non-zero status, throws luabind::cast_failed unless `lua_type(L, -1) == 3`, and answers `lua_tointeger(L, -1)` - to the nearest, ties to even - cutting the stack back. One caller, GetOfferTradeScoreFromLua (0xA0DF24). `ret 4` at 0xA44309.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA44210..0xA44309: `push 1; push 7; push edi; call ecx` at 0xA44255..0xA4425A, the lua_type test `sub eax, 3` at 0xA442A9 and the throw with ThrowInfo 0x164B1E4 at 0xA442BD, lua_tointeger through [0xD2B4D4] at 0xA442DF. One caller by findRefs.

addresses.name: LuaCallProxy_LicenceTechnology_CallIntResult
addresses.comment: The five-argument twin of LuaCallProxy_CallIntResult, for `DiploScore_LicenceTechnology`: called flag at +0x20, arguments through LuaPushArgs_LicenceTechnology (0x6457B0), pcall with **(L, 5, 1)**, the same error, type and lua_tointeger handling. One caller, GetLicenceTechnologyScoreFromLua (0xA44ABC). `ret 4` at 0xA452BB; the code after it, from 0xA452C0, is another function.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA451C0..0xA452BB: `mov byte [ebx+0x20], 1`, call 0xA457B0, `push 1; push 5` at 0xA45207. One caller by findRefs.

addresses.name: LuaPushArgs_OfferTrade
addresses.comment: Pushes DiploScore_OfferTrade's seven arguments out of the proxy's slots: the CEU3AI - **nil when null**, else a Lua-derived self if `__RTDynamicCast` to luabind::wrap_base finds one, else a pointer instance (0x514660), no copy - then actor, recipient and observer **each as a fresh copy** through LuaPush_CCountryTagByValue (0x5137C0), then LuaPush_TradeActionAndGoods (0x645B60) for the action and the two goods blocks. Bare `ret` at 0xA44DC8. Two callers, the int call (0xA4424A) and the proxy's destructor (0xA441A7).
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA44D50..0xA44DC8: three calls to 0x5137C0 on [ebx+4], [ebx+8], [ebx+0xC], then 0xA45B60 with EAX = ebx+0x10. The proxy's slots are filled by BuildLuaCallProxy_DiploScore_OfferTrade (0xA44646..0xA4466D) in the order &ai, actor, recipient, observer, &action, traded_from, traded_to.

addresses.name: LuaPush_TradeActionAndGoods
addresses.comment: **`voTradeAction` is the CTradeAction itself, by pointer.** Pushes the action as nil when null, else through the wrap_base test (type descriptor 0x17478B8 `.?AVCTradeAction@@`) and a pointer instance (0x990F40) - no copy, so the script holds the very action being answered and `GetRoute()` reaches its embedded route. Then LuaPush_TwoGoodsValues (0x645EE0) for `voTradedFrom` and `voTradedTo`. Bare `ret`s. One caller, LuaPushArgs_OfferTrade.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA45B60..0xA45BDD: [edi] dereferenced and tested, __RTDynamicCast(esi, 0, 0x17478B8, 0x17147E8, 0), the pointer push 0x990F40 at 0xA45BC5, then 0xA45EE0 on every path. Wrong if 0x990F40 copied the object; it is the converter the other pointer pushes use (FINDINGS-luahost.md).

addresses.name: LuaPush_TwoGoodsValues
addresses.comment: Copies each of two seven-float blocks (28 bytes, `[edi]` then `[edi+4]`) into a local and pushes it through LuaPush_CGoodsValuesCopy (0x646230) - so `voTradedFrom` and `voTradedTo` are **CGoodsValues objects of their own**, and writing to one changes nothing in the engine. Bare `ret` at 0xA45F68. Three callers, the three arms of LuaPush_TradeActionAndGoods.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA45EE0..0xA45F68: two movq/movq/movq/mov copies of 0x1C bytes, each followed by call 0xA46230.

addresses.name: LuaPush_CGoodsValuesCopy
addresses.signature: void __cdecl LuaPush_CGoodsValuesCopy(const float* value@ESI, lua_State* L@stack:4, int policy_a@stack:8, int policy_b@stack:0xC)
addresses.comment: `operator new(0x1C)`, a copy of the 28 bytes at ESI, and the new object pushed as an auto_ptr-held CGoodsValues (0xA463A0): a fresh userdata each time. 0x1C is the size of CGoodsValues - seven floats. The two trailing stack dwords are an empty policy object passed by value and are not read here. Bare `ret` at 0xA462B2. Two callers, both in LuaPush_TwoGoodsValues.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA46230..0xA4627D: push 0x1C / call 0xB9602F, the copy from [esi] .. [esi+0x18], then 0xA463A0 with the holder. The size agrees with the seven def_readwrite float fields luabind.json gives CGoodsValues (offsets 0..24).

addresses.comment: **`voCommand` is the CLicenceTechnologyAction itself, by pointer**: pushes the observer tag as a fresh copy (0x5137C0), then the action - nil when null, else the wrap_base test (type descriptor 0x1747C70 `.?AVCLicenceTechnologyAction@@`) and a pointer instance (0xA46010), no copy. Bare `ret`s, the last at 0xA45CF5. One caller, LuaPushArgs_LicenceTechnology.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA45CA0..0xA45CF5; the type descriptor's name read at 0x1747C78.

addresses.name: BuildLuaCallProxy_AiAndTag
addresses.signature: void* __cdecl BuildLuaCallProxy_AiAndTag(const char* lua_function@EAX, lua_State* L@EDI, void* proxy@ESI, void* ai_slot@stack:4, CCountryTag* tag@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: Builds the void call `lua_function(ai, tag)` that CCountry::RunHourlyAITrade makes for `ProposeTrades` and `EvalutateExistingTrades`: lua_pushstring and lua_gettable on the globals, then the proxy's L, called flag 1, `[+8]` luabind::detail::pcall, the two argument pointers at +0xC and +0x10 and the terminator at +0x14. Answers the proxy. The call itself is made by LuaCallProxy_AiAndTag_CallVoid (0x10D600). Bare `ret` at 0x5102BD; the `ret 8` bodies after it are other functions.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x510280..0x5102BD; its one caller 0x4DC7D8 loads EAX with 'ProposeTrades' (0x15C0FCC) or, by the jump from 0x4DC827, 'EvalutateExistingTrades' (0x15C0FDC), pushes the tag (country+0xCA4) and &ai, and cleans 8 bytes.

addresses.name: LuaPushArgs_AiAndTag
addresses.comment: Pushes (CEU3AI*, CCountryTag): the AI as nil, a Lua-derived self or a pointer instance (0x514660), and the tag as a **fresh copy** through LuaPush_CCountryTagByValue (0x5137C0). The template twin of LuaPushArgs_CountryAndTag (0x111830). Bare `ret`s at 0x511A8E and 0x511AAB. One caller, LuaCallProxy_AiAndTag_CallVoid.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x511A40..0x511AAB; findRefs --callers: one call, 0x50D627.

addresses.name: LuaCallProxy_AiAndTag_CallVoid
addresses.comment: The destructor of luabind's `proxy_function_caller<void, (CEU3AI*, CCountryTag)>`, where the void call is made: if the called flag (+0x14) is clear, set it, push the two arguments (LuaPushArgs_AiAndTag, 0x111A40), pcall with **(L, 2, 0)** and throw luabind::error on a non-zero status. One caller, CCountry::RunHourlyAITrade at 0x4DC7E0, whose try block catches the error and reports it (ReportLuaError at 0x4DC82F) - so a Lua error in ProposeTrades or EvalutateExistingTrades ends that country's hour quietly, and the next hour draws again. Bare `ret` at 0x50D683.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x50D600..0x50D683: `cmp byte [esi+0x14], 0`, call 0x511A40, `push 0; push 2` at 0x50D632. ehcatches 0x4DC410: one try, .?AVerror@luabind@@; handler 0x4DC829 calls 0xAA8050 and resumes at 0x4DC7E5.

addresses.name: InitTradeGoodsEpsilon
addresses.comment: The `.CRT$XCU` static initialiser that writes g_TradeGoodsEpsilon (rva 0x17148A0) as `(int)floorf(1.5f)` = **1**, off the float 1.5 at VA 0x17179AC, through floorf (0x1FD0) and _ftol2_sse (0x808870) - trap 8's third case. Its address is held once, at VA 0xD44600 in the initialiser table; no direct caller. So the 'threshold' CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingDisabledResource and IsTradeingAwayNeededResource compare against is one thousandth, and no define moves it.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xD0C240..0xD0C260; the float read at 0x17179AC is 1.5; holders: the one data reference at 0xD44600. findRefs --address 0x1B148A0: three references, this writer and the two predicates' reads at 0x89B41D and 0x89B48E.

addresses.name: g_TradeGoodsEpsilon
addresses.no_signature: a global int, not a function
addresses.comment: int, **1** (one thousandth), written once at start-up by InitTradeGoodsEpsilon (rva 0x90C240) as `(int)floorf(1.5f)`. Read by CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingDisabledResource (an amount counts when above it) and CEU3AI::IsTradeingAwayNeededResource (a balance counts as short when below minus it). Not a define.
addresses.evidence: findRefs --address 0x1B148A0: exactly three code references - the writer at 0xD0C25B and the readers at 0x89B41D and 0x89B48E. Wrong if a second writer existed outside .text; the address is in .data's zero-fill and only code writes there.

addresses.name: CCountry::AIGetTradeRoutes
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name (registered `CArray<CTradeRoute*>& AIGetTradeRoutes() const` with return_clausewitz_iterator). **It rebuilds a scratch vector on every call**: it empties the std::vector<CTradeRoute*> at CCountry +0x34/+0x38/+0x3C, then walks the country's CDiplomacyStatus array (+0xE28 .. +0xE2C), **one status per country id from 0 up**, and appends every route on each status's trade_routes list (+0x60) in list order - active and inactive alike - and answers `this + 0x34`. So EvalutateExistingTrades walks the country's routes ordered by the other country's id. Being a member, the vector is overwritten by the next call on the same country. Bare `ret` at 0x508218.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x5080C0..0x508160: `lea esi, [ecx+0x34]`, the erase of [esi]..[esi+4] through 0xB95B00, the loop bound `(+0xE2C - +0xE28) >> 2` and `[status+0x60]` list head; Ghidra 0x5080C0 shows the push_back with its self-aliasing test and the grow at 0x4C0700. One luabind registration and no data reference holds the address.

addresses.name: CTechnologyStatus::IsUnitAvailable
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name. **True when the country has unlocked the unit type and the type's usable_by admits it**: `this->unit_available (+0x27C)[unit->Index (+0x24)]` and SubUnitDefinitionIsUsableBy(this->country (+0x248)->tag (+0xCA4), unit). Both must hold. A null unit is dereferenced, not refused. `ret 4` at 0x533052 and 0x533059.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x533020..0x533059 entire. One luabind registration, no data reference.

addresses.name: CCountryTag::IsReal
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name. **False only for the rebels**: compares the tag's three letters with 'R', 'E', 'B' and answers false on a full match, true otherwise - the null tag `---` and a country that does not exist are 'real' by this test. Bare `ret`s at 0x479733 and 0x479736.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x479720..0x479736 entire (cmp [ecx], 0x52; [ecx+1], 0x45; [ecx+2], 0x42). One luabind registration, no data reference.

addresses.name: CGoodsPool::GetFloat
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name. `fild [this + 8 + category*4]; fdiv 1000.0; fstp dword` - the pool's thousandths over 1000, **rounded to a single-precision float**, exactly as CFixedPoint:Get() does it, so `pool:GetFloat(g)` and `pool:Get(g):Get()` agree. `ret 4` at 0x8E81B7.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x8E81A0..0x8E81B7 entire; 1000.0 is the double at 0x160A300. One luabind registration, no data reference.

addresses.name: CTradeAction::SetTrading
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTradeAction::SetTrading(CTradeAction* this, CFixedPoint* value, GoodsCategory category)
addresses.evidence: disasm 0xA38DF0..0xA38ED1. The locals after `push edi`: [esp+0x10] recipient letters, [esp+0x14] recipient id, [esp+0x18]/[esp+0x1C] the actor. On the negative path `push -1` then `mov [esp+0x18], edx` (edx = actor id) and, after three more pushes, `mov [esp+0x20], ecx` (ecx = actor letters) both land on the recipient slot; the one call that follows (0xA38EB6) passes `lea edx, [esp+0x14]` = that slot. Wrong if the helpers 0xB99AF0/0xB99980 popped other than 16 bytes each (they are the stdcall _allmul/_alldiv the record names).

addresses.name: CEU3AI::GetSpamPenalty
addresses.signature: float __thiscall CEU3AI::GetSpamPenalty(CEU3AI* this, const CCountryTag* tag)
addresses.comment:
The game's own Lua name, from the baked-in registration at 0x8F6691 whose RTTI type is `float CEU3AI::GetSpamPenalty(const CCountryTag&)`. 0x89B530 to the `ret 4` at 0x89B63B. **Nought for any country nobody plays**: it indexes played_countries_array (g_CCurrentGameState +0xBCC) by the tag's id and answers 0.0 where that is zero (`fldz` at 0x89B55A). Otherwise, with this AI's own country (CEU3AI +0x20) and its CDiplomacyStatus toward the tag (+0xE28[id]):

    dNow  = (tick - 43800000) / 24                 toward nought; tick = state +0xBDC
    dNext = (status->next_offer_allowed (+0x50) - 43800000) / 24
    days  = dNext - dNow + 24                       by way of whole years of 365.0 (0x160A550),
                                                    which cancel exactly
    penalty = (float)(int)((float)max(days, 0) * 10.0f)   10.0f at 0x171DBB0

so **ten points for every day from now until 24 days after next_offer_allowed** - the end of this AI's own seven-day cooldown on that player: 310 the hour this AI proposes to him (next_offer_allowed is that proposal's date + 168 h), 240 when the cooldown ends, nought 24 days later. The answer is a float holding a whole number. *Revised 2026-10-13 from `likely`: the rest of the body is read.*
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x89B530..0x89B63B: the gate at 0x89B547..0x89B55A; GetCountry on this+0x20 at 0x89B568; [status+0x50] at 0x89B57F; the /24 by magic 0x2AAAAAAB with sar 2; the year terms at 0x89B5B1..0x89B60E; `lea esi, [ebx+esi+0x18]`, the clamp at 0x89B616 and mulss [0x171DBB0] (= 10.0). The doubles read: [0x160A550] = 365.0. Wrong if dNow and dNext were swapped - ecx (the tick) is subtracted and esi (the status) added.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingDisabledResource
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name, from the registration at 0x8EFCA3, and the fourth gate inside CTradeAction::GetAIAcceptance (called at 0xA38B64 on the **recipient's** CEU3AI, with the action's embedded route) - a true answer makes the trade's AI acceptance zero. `this` is never read. It walks the routes on `countries[route->from_id]->+0xE28[route->to_id]`'s trade_routes (+0x60), **looking only at inactive ones** (+0x54 set, the `cmp byte [edx+0x54], 0` at 0x89B425), and answers true at the first inactive route and good g other than money (index 2 is skipped) where **both the candidate and that route move more than g_TradeGoodsEpsilon (one thousandth) of g in the same block** - both +0x34 blocks, or both +0x44 blocks. The blocks are matched **by position, not by country**: an inactive route made the other way round (its `from` the candidate's `to`) is compared from-block to from-block all the same. So an AI refuses a trade in a good that a stalled route between the same pair already carries the same way. *Revised 2026-10-13: the threshold is 1, from InitTradeGoodsEpsilon (rva 0x90C240), and the comparison is spelled out.*
addresses.evidence: Ghidra 0x89B3E0 and disasm 0x89B3E0..0x89B472: `iVar3 != 2` and the four `[0x1B148A0] < value` tests joined as (a.to && b.to) || (a.from && b.from); the global written only by 0xD0C240 as (int)floorf(1.5f). Wrong if the existing route's blocks were swapped to the candidate's orientation before the test - there is no from_id comparison in the loop.

addresses.name: CCountry::RunHourlyAITrade
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x4DC6E5..0x4DC839: `cmp byte [esi+0xDA4], 0`, `cmp [ecx+0x1D8], ebx`, the player test at 0x4DC701..0x4DC71E (edi = GetLocalPlayer, reloaded at 0x4DC666), call 0xAA2B90 / idiv 6 at 0x4DC7A9..0x4DC7B8, and at 0x4DC7F8 a **second** call 0xAA2B90 / idiv 10; ehcatches 0x4DC410 and the handler at 0x4DC829. Wrong if 0x4DC7F8 were reached with the first draw's remainder still in a register - it opens with a fresh call.

addresses.name: GetOfferTradeScoreFromLua
addresses.signature: int __cdecl GetOfferTradeScoreFromLua(CCountryTag* actor, CCountryTag* recipient, CCountryTag* observer, CTradeAction* action, float* traded_from, float* traded_to, CCountryTag recipient_value)
addresses.comment: The widest clone of GetDiploScoreFromLua, sitting immediately after it (the bridge's last `ret` is at 0xA0DDE1) with `DiploScore_OfferTrade` reached through the proxy at 0xA44610. Eight stack dwords, `add esp, 0x20` at its one caller, CTradeAction::GetAIAcceptance, which passes **the recipient as the observer too**. Same player/0x1A8562F short-circuit as the bridge, and the same choice of AI: the recipient's CEU3AI, else the actor's. Seven values go to Lua, through LuaCallProxy_OfferTrade_CallIntResult (0x644210) and LuaPushArgs_OfferTrade (0x644D50): the CEU3AI, three fresh tag copies, **the CTradeAction itself by pointer**, and **two fresh CGoodsValues** - `voTradedFrom` is the route's +0x44 block (what the route's `from`, the actor, hands over each day) and `voTradedTo` its +0x34 block (what the recipient hands over). GetAIAcceptance has laid each out in **CGoodsValues order, not goods order** - vMoney, vFuel, vCrudeOil, vMetal, vEnergy, vRareMaterials, vSupplies at +0..+0x18, i.e. goods 2, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 0 - each `(float)((double)(float)thousandths / 1000.0)`. The answer is the script's number to the nearest integer, ties to even. **A Lua error answers 0**: the one try block catches luabind::error, ReportLuaError (0x6A8050) at 0xA0DF4C, and the resume at 0xA0DF57 is `xor eax, eax`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md and FINDINGS-tradeaid.md.
addresses.evidence: CTradeAction::GetAIAcceptance 0xA38B6D..0xA38D03: block [esi+0x6C] (route+0x44) stored [0]->esp+0x44, [1]->+0x30, [2]->+0x2C, [3]->+0x34, [4]->+0x38, [5]->+0x3C, [6]->+0x40, and the pointer pushed is esp+0x2C - money first; block [esi+0x5C] likewise to esp+0x10..0x28, pointer esp+0x10. The pushes: recipient by value, &B, &A, this, this+0x10, this+0x10, this+8. luabind.json's def_readwrite offsets for CGoodsValues give vMoney 0, vFuel 4, vCrudeOil 8, vMetal 12, vEnergy 16, vRareMaterials 20, vSupplies 24 - two independent sources agreeing. ehcatches 0xA0DDF0: one try, luabind::error.

structs.name: CGoodsValues
structs.comment: Seven floats a script reads by name - vMoney, vFuel, vCrudeOil, vMetal, vEnergy, vRareMaterials, vSupplies at +0 .. +0x18 (the fields come from the Lua half, luabind.json's def_readwrite). **Not in goods order**: goods index 2 (money) is first and index 0 (supplies) last. What the engine hands DiploScore_OfferTrade as voTradedFrom and voTradedTo, each a fresh copy (LuaPush_CGoodsValuesCopy, rva 0x646230). Goods per day, as floats.
structs.evidence: LuaPush_CGoodsValuesCopy allocates exactly 0x1C and copies 0x1C bytes (0xA46249..0xA46276); the seven def_readwrite offsets end at 24 with a 4-byte float. No vftable: the class has a type descriptor (0x1747728) only because luabind registers it.

struct_fields.name: ai_trade_routes
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a std::vector<CTradeRoute*> that CCountry::AIGetTradeRoutes (rva 0x1080C0) empties and refills on every call with every route on every one of the country's CDiplomacyStatus objects, in id order, and hands to Lua as `CArray<CTradeRoute*>&`. Scratch: nothing else is known to read it.
struct_fields.evidence: AIGetTradeRoutes: `lea esi, [ecx+0x34]`, the erase of [esi]..[esi+4] and the push_back against [esi+4]/[esi+8], `return this + 0x34`; the registration's return type is CArray<CTradeRoute*>&. Not otherwise searched for, so 'nothing else reads it' is unchecked.

struct_fields.name: ai_trade_routes_end
struct_fields.evidence: AIGetTradeRoutes: the erase writes it back to begin at 0x5080F3, the push_back stores through it and adds 4.

struct_fields.name: ai_trade_routes_capacity
struct_fields.comment: Capacity of the ai_trade_routes vector (+0x34); compared against the end before the grow through 0x4C0700.
